title.text: PantryPulse: five UI directions, every page

how.text:
How to use
Press Play on a board, then use its menu to visit all 7 pages: Overview, Data Explorer, Recommendations, Scenario Lab, Import data, Methodology, Settings.
On Overview, tap a site to open its panel.
All numbers are fictional sample data.

mix.text:
Chosen mix (Gabriel)
Pantry Ledger's structure with Market Fresh's accents.

FROM 2: paper tones, serif headings and story, ruled lines, menu across the top.
FROM 4: leaf-green accent, sage tints, pill buttons and badges, tomato red for danger, green land on the map.

PROS
- Calm and crafted, and clearly about food
- Green action color is easy to spot on paper

CONS
- Green accent must never mean 'OK' by itself; OK stays neutral
- Amends the art direction (teal becomes green, serif added)

n1.text:
1 · Calm Desk (style: Minimal)
Today's brand, decluttered.

PROS
- Least rework before the W6 candidate
- Most legible; plain sans everywhere
- Matches the approved art direction

CONS
- The least distinctive
- Reads as a good tool, not a crafted one

n2.text:
2 · Pantry Ledger (style: Minimal, editorial)
A stock ledger: paper tones, serif headings, ruled lines, menu across the top.

PROS
- Calm, like reading a briefing
- Top menu gives the map and tables full width
- Same Plex type family as today

CONS
- Serif reads slower at small sizes
- Top menu has less room if pages are added
- Amends the art direction

n3.text:
3 · Night Dispatch (style: Dark)
A dispatch room: dark by default, list floating over an edge-to-edge map.

PROS
- Most striking; the map is the hero
- Danger colors stand out on dark
- Easy on the eyes in long sessions

CONS
- Floating list can cover markers
- Dark tables are harder to print and read in daylight
- Biggest departure; every screen needs a dark pass

n4.text:
4 · Market Fresh (style: Pastel)
Produce-aisle greens, rounded cards, larger type.

PROS
- Friendliest for volunteers and first-time users
- Clearly about food
- Large targets, roomy layout

CONS
- Green accent sits close to 'OK' meaning; risk colors need care
- Roomier layout shows fewer rows
- Can feel less serious for retail planners

n5.text:
5 · Crate Label (style: Neobrutalism)
Shipping-crate labels: heavy outlines, stencil caps, hard shadows.

PROS
- Most memorable identity; strong warehouse feel
- Very high contrast
- Sections are unmistakable

CONS
- Loudest; works against the 'calm, not dense' goal
- All-caps labels scan slower
- Heavy borders compete with the map
